chunks: Among that, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Ubayd Allah ibn al-Marzaban, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I visited Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) the year before he went to Iraq, and his son Ali was sitting in front of him. He looked at me and said: 'O Muhammad, indeed there will be a movement/disturbance in this year, so do not be anxious about it.' I said: 'And what will it be, may God make me your ransom? For it has filled me with anxiety.' He said: 'I will go to this despot, and indeed he will not initiate any evil from me, nor from the one who will be after me.' I said: 'And what will it be, may God make me your ransom?' He said: 'God will make the unjust err and do what He wills.' I said: 'And what is that, may God make me your ransom?' He said: 'Whoever wrongs this son of mine and denies his Imamate after me is like the one who wronged Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and denied his right after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said: 'By God, if God prolongs my life, I will submit to his right and affirm his Imamate.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. God will prolong your life, and you will submit to his right (peace be upon him) and affirm his Imamate and the Imamate of the one who will be after him.' I said: 'And who is that?' He said: 'His son, Muhammad.' I said: 'To him be the pleasure and submission.'

key_terms.الطَّاغِيَةِ: The despot (referring to the Abbasid ruler)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Musa al-Kadhim designate as his successor and the next Imam after him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi* (via Tusi’s *Al-Ghayba*) establishes the explicit designation (Nass) of Imam Ali al-Rida, emphasizing the continuity of the Imamate through his son Muhammad al-Jawad. The Imam draws a parallel between the denial of Ali al-Rida’s right and the historical denial of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib’s right after the Prophet, underscoring the theological weight of accepting the designated successor. This narrative serves as a key proof for the Twelver Shia doctrine of the infallible Imamate passing directly from father to son.
